title: Headnotes record, v1
description: One line of runs/<run_id>/records/<court_id>/<yyyy>.jsonl: the headnotes one run produced for one CourtListener decision (cluster). The first block of fields is the envelope every record kind shares; `headnotes` is this kind's payload.

cluster_id.description: CourtListener opinion-cluster id. The key for joining across runs and kinds.

run_id.description: Must equal the run_id in the run's run.json (and its folder name).

court_id.description: CourtListener court id (ca1 ... ca11, cadc, cafc, scotus, ...). Decides the shard folder.

date_filed.description: CourtListener date_filed, YYYY-MM-DD. Its year decides the shard file. null only when CourtListener has none (shard: unknown.jsonl).

case_name.description: Optional, for people reading the file.

citation.description: Optional lead citation, for people reading the file.

opinion_id.description: CourtListener opinion id whose text was sent to the model, when known.

status.description: ok: headnotes for real holdings. no_holding: the text decides nothing (bare affirmance, order, certification); one headnote saying what was ordered, empty slugs, to be dropped from the graph. failed: the producer gave no usable answer; headnotes is empty and error says why.

input.description: What the model saw. Optional; the run manifest describes the input in general.

truncated.description: True when the text was cut before sending.

request_id.description: The producer's own id for the request (e.g. a Batches custom_id).

extra.description: Producer-specific fields that are not part of the shared format (ranks, notes, flags). Free-form; nothing downstream may depend on it.

text.description: The rule of law, in general terms. Word limit is set by the run's prompt, not here.

concept_slugs.description: Up to 3 taxonomy slugs; may be empty. Whether they come from the real taxonomy is recorded in run.json (taxonomy.verified).

first_paragraph.description: First paragraph of the opinion this headnote rests on, in the numbering named by run.json (input.paragraph_numbering).

anchors.description: Optional: the first words of the first and last cited paragraphs, to find them when numbering differs between runs.
